findings.reason: clause 2's headline "median gate share" is inflated for the overlapping runs unless the plan states a deduplication rule or a precedence (use `test_logs`, else the armed-suite paths, deduped by path).
findings.text: the new mechanism takes "each gate's duration from the gate logs the run cites (test_logs, baseline_suite.log_path, after_suite.log_path)", but these sources name the same files: for the cited control run, `test_logs` is `gate-after.log, gate-base.log` while `baseline_suite.log_path` is `gate-base.log` and `after_suite.log_path` is `gate-after.log`, so a scanner enumerating all three reads each arm twice and roughly doubles that run's gate share — and the overlap is systematic, 32 of the 112 most recent runs citing gate logs (29%) name a log under both `test_logs` and `baseline_suite/after_suite.log_path`

findings.reason: the plan should require the fraction of gate-share figures taken from the fallback to be reported beside the median (or the fallback-sourced runs separated), because the instruction "say for each figure which source it came from" is per-figure and leaves a mixed-source median uninterpretable.
findings.text: the changed mechanism falls back to foreground tool-call wall time whenever no cited log reports a duration, but that fallback is exactly the source the same bullet discredits ("tool-call time alone would miss exactly the long gates this plan is about"), and it is not a rare edge: in a sample of the 80 most recent runs, 24 of the 58 citing any gate log cited a log with no "in N s"-style duration (non-pytest gates, and truncated gates that print no pytest summary), so a substantial share of the per-lane median rests on the rejected source
